### Investment Memo: EFX — October 21, 2026

**Verdict**: HOLD (Initiate starter position only) | Conviction: Medium-Low
**Price Target**: $175 (~0% vs. current $176.54); base-case IV $170, range $150–$185
**Time Horizon**: 12–24 months

**Investment Thesis**
Equifax is a narrow-moat data oligopolist whose crown jewel — The Work Number / Workforce Solutions (44% operating margin, effectively all of company operating income) — remains intact and growing, while the market has de-rated the stock 41% peak-to-trough on a live federal rulemaking (FHFA bi-merge) that could structurally re-price the mortgage credit product. At $176.54 the stock trades ~4% *above* our base-case intrinsic value and *at* consensus target after a +28.6% three-week rally — the de-rating is largely rational, not a mispricing. This is a quality franchise at a fair price with an unmodelable binary policy risk: own a small starter, preserve capital for ≤$155/≤$140.

---

**Key Findings by Domain**

- **Macro & Sector**: Sector ATTRACTIVE (mature 3-firm oligopoly, ~6% market CAGR, extreme barriers, late-trough mortgage cycle = asymmetric optionality). But macro regime is UNFAVOURABLE now: Fed hiked Sept-26, 10Y at 5.15%, 30Y mortgage 7.40% (+142bp from Feb) printed *after* quarter-end — Q4 mortgage likely worse than Q3's $20M hit. Bull surprise: term-premium reversal could deliver $210–230.
- **Geopolitical & Legal**: Composite MEDIUM. No Russia/China exposure (genuine positive). Binding constraint is Washington: $130M FCRA accruals booked ($100M coding-error settlement, final approval Jan-27; $30M inquiry-dispute, Dec-26), FHFA bi-merge now in formal rulemaking, EU AI Act treats credit scoring as high-risk.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Value**: HOLD. IV ≈ $170 ($150–$185). FCF $1.10B (5.3% yield), ROIC ~11% vs WACC ~9% — thin spread. 20.8x FY26E adj. EPS is the cheapest in a decade, but rationally so: mortgage-score pricing is being regulated into a $1 commodity. Buy aggressively ≤$140; trim >$200.
- **Equity Fundamentals — Growth**: BUY (moderate). EPS CAGR ~11% ($8.50→$13.00 by 2030), 7/7 consecutive EPS beats, Vitality Index >17%, $150M AI productivity program, FCF margin 18.7%→21%+. ~13–15% IRR if the 21x multiple merely holds. Rule of 40 ~26–30 is the knock; aggressive buyer $150–160.
- **Quantitative Signals**: NEUTRAL, upgrade bias. 47th percentile composite: Value 73rd pct (P/FCF 19.3 cheapest in comp set), Momentum 20th pct — but momentum misses the 14-session +28.6% reversal. Alpha t-stat −0.63 = noise; ρ to SPY only 0.174. Sector-wide de-rating, not idiosyncratic.
- **Financial Risk**: MODERATE. Net debt/EBITDA 2.50x, coverage 5.4x, S&P 'BBB'; 2026/27 maturity cliff neutralized (short-term debt $1.41B→$158M; revolver upsized to $2.0B). Red flag: buybacks + dividends $1.41B = **128% of FCF**, debt-funded. Cash thin ($193M). Goodwill 68% of assets (+$1.18B in Q3).
- **Non-Financial Risk**: HIGH. Repeat-mode accuracy/dispute failures ($700M breach, $15M CFPB penalty, $100M score-error settlement, open CFPB probe into The Work Number — same control theme, four times in eight years). FHFA bi-merge is a live process, not a tail risk. Zero insider purchases through a 40% drawdown. Governance itself clean (independent chair, no fraud flags).
- **ESG**: AVERAGE / investment implication NEUTRAL. Environmental low-risk (SBTi net-zero, cloud migration). Social structurally high — the product is other people's PII. No cyber/accuracy modifier in comp plan. Worth ~0.5–1.0x EBITDA multiple discount; not a catalyst either way.
- **Alternative Data**: NEUTRAL, low confidence. News sentiment +0.714 and consumer search interest +20% y/y are price-confirming; revenue growth decelerating 14.3%→10.6%→9.6%→~7.9% implied Q4, surprise magnitude compressing (+10%→+2.7%). The beat is priced after the rally.
- **Short / Contrarian View**: Earnings quality MEDIUM-HIGH — clean books (OCF/NI 2.45x), deteriorating economics. Diluted EPS is **12% below 2021** despite +23% revenue; FY26 consensus implies a 34.6% EBITDA margin vs. 30.8% actual — an all-time record. GAAP-to-adjusted gap 44%. Three consecutive quarters of growth deceleration.

---

**Bull Case**
- **Workforce Solutions moat intact**: 44% margins, +7% growth, $550M state-agency ACV — counter-cyclical, contracted, effectively un-replicable payroll data.
- **Mortgage optionality un-priced**: mortgage revenue +15% in Q3 into a shrinking market (share gain); a 100bp rate retrace flips the biggest headwind to a 300–500bp tailwind at high incremental margin.
- **Cheapest quality asset in the cohort**: 12.8x EV/EBITDA vs. 16.3x peer median, 20.8x forward EPS, FCF $1.1B — with $150M AI cost savings cushioning the cycle.

**Bear Case**
- **FHFA bi-merge / $1 VantageScore pricing** structurally cuts revenue-per-origination in the highest-margin product line — a policy decision outside management control, now in formal rulemaking.
- **Margin recovery is promised, not proven**: operating margin 18.0% vs. 23.1% in 2021; consensus needs ~380bp of one-year expansion to a record. EPS growth is partly buyback arithmetic (share count −5.5%) with returns running at 128% of FCF.
- **Macro tape hostile**: 7.40% mortgage (post-quarter-end), Fed hiking, USD 121.4 — three of four transmission channels negative and intensifying.

**Key Risks**
1. FHFA finalizes bi-merge/two-bureau rule (structural, permanent — exit trigger, don't wait for price).
2. Second guidance cut on mortgage (Q4 exposed to the 7.40% print).
3. Workforce Solutions organic growth <5% or adverse CFPB action against The Work Number — that segment *is* the P&L.
4. Score-price commoditization outpacing volume offset → gross margin <55%.
5. Capital allocation: leverage >3.0x while buybacks continue; goodwill impairment (68% of assets).

**Portfolio Construction Note**
Initiate **1.0% starter**, hard cap 2.5%, on a limit ladder: 0.5% now (limit ≤$168), +0.75% at ≤$155, +0.75% at ≤$140 — or pay up only on a confirming FY27 guide (≥8% revenue growth with margin expansion) at the **Feb 3, 2027 print; do not exceed 1.0% before it** (8–12% earnings-day gaps). Size on 44% volatility, not conviction. EFX–TRU correlation 0.86 — cap the credit-data sleeve at 5%, EFX+TRU ≤3%; exclude EFX from Industrials sleeve counts (misclassification). Stop $131 close-basis (discipline device, not protection). Trim one-third at $205–210; cut to ≤0.75% core ≥$225. Thesis-invalidation exits per the seven rules above — FHFA final rule is the one event where we sell first and reassess.

**Data gaps flagged**: beta conflict (0.59 vs 1.34 — we use 1.2–1.3); Moody's rating unconfirmed; no revenue-by-country disclosure; Q3-26 acquisition terms inferred from goodwill step-up; FHFA NPRM timing unknown; MSCI/Sustainalytics scores unverified. None are thesis-breaking; all are noted for follow-up.

# EFX — Portfolio Construction Recommendation
**Equifax Inc. | Price $176.54 (20-Oct-26) | Mkt cap ~$20.7B | EV ~$25.7B**
**Synthesizing 11 specialist reports** (no dedicated dividend/income report was filed; the income angle is covered inside Financial Risk and Value)

---

## 1. Agent Conviction Summary

| Agent | View | Conviction | Key Finding |

| **Alt Data Analyst** | **NEUTRAL**, low confidence | Low | Sentiment +0.714 and 7/7 beats, but revenue growth decelerating 14.3% → 9.6% → **~7.9% implied**; the beat is priced |

---

## 2. Consensus Assessment

**Agreement level: LOW on price/timing — MEDIUM on business quality.**

Everyone agrees on the *asset*: a three-firm oligopoly with an irreplaceable payroll-verification franchise (Workforce Solutions, 44% operating margin, producing essentially the whole company's operating income) and 55%+ gross margins. **Zero agents allege fraud, accounting manipulation, or solvency risk.** Quant's accruals score (−8.05%, cash conversion 2.4x) and Short's 2.45x OCF/NI independently confirm the books are clean.

The split is entirely about **what you pay and when**:

- **Constructive (2):** Growth, Sector.
- **Neutral / unconfirmed (4):** Quant, Alt Data, ESG, Short.
- **Cautionary (5):** Value ("not at this price"), Macro, Non-Financial Risk, Geo/Legal, Financial Risk.

**Conflict resolution — three cases, resolved:**

1. **Growth BUY vs Value HOLD.** These are not actually in conflict. Growth says "be an aggressive buyer at $150–160." Value says "buy at ≤$140, IV is $170." **Both imply $176.54 is too high.** I resolve toward the caution: the two most price-disciplined agents converge on a materially lower entry.

2. **Sector ATTRACTIVE vs Macro UNFAVOURABLE.** Sector is looking at the mortgage cycle (late-trough, optionality un-priced); Macro is looking at the *rate regime* that determines when that trough ends. Macro's 7.40% mortgage print occurred **after** quarter-end, meaning Q4's $20M mortgage hit is already stale-good. The cycle is not turning on a 2–3 quarter view — Macro wins the near-term, Sector wins the 2027–28 view. That argues for **staged entry, not a full position**.

3. **Short Analyst vs the bull case.** Per my framework, a fraud/risk flag outranks a bullish value view. This is *not* a fraud flag — so no veto. But it earns a **haircut to the Growth model**: consensus requires ~380bp of one-year EBITDA margin expansion to an all-time record, in a business whose operating margin has *fallen* 510bp since 2021. I discount Growth's 11.2% EPS CAGR to ~8–9% for sizing, which is what drops expected return from ~13–15% to ~10–11%.

**Net: a high-quality franchise at approximately fair value, carrying one live binary policy risk and an unfavourable macro tape. Conviction tier: MODERATE-LOW (~55/100).**

---

## 3. Position Sizing Recommendation

### Initiate at **1.0% of portfolio**; authorized to build to a **2.5% hard cap**

**Kelly arithmetic (fractional):**
| Scenario | Probability | Return from $176.54 |
|---|---|---|
| Bull — 10Y retraces, mortgage thaws, margin recovery | 35% | +25% ($220) |
| Base — multiple holds ~21x, EPS compounds 8–9% | 40% | 0% ($170–185) |
| Bear — bi-merge NPRM or second guidance cut | 25% | −22% ($137 retest) |
| **Expected value** | | **+3.3%** |

Full Kelly = edge/variance = 0.033 / 0.193 ≈ 17% — **absurd for a single name.** Applying ~1/10 fractional Kelly for a 44%-vol name with an unmodelable binary regulatory risk gives ~1.7%, then haircutting for the live FHFA rulemaking (which cannot be priced by any model I have) yields **1.0–1.5%**. I set the starter at the bottom of that range and hold the rest as a pre-authorized add ladder.

**Why not 3%?** Because at 44% annualized volatility, a 1.0% weight already contributes ~0.44% of portfolio volatility — equivalent to a 2.5% position in a normal 18%-vol equity. **Size on volatility, not on conviction.**

**Why not pass?** Because the bear-case floor is a $137 retest (−22%) against a bull case of +25% to $220, the balance sheet is investment grade, FCF is durable at $1.1B, and the market is paying 12.8x EV/EBITDA for a 30%-EBITDA-margin data oligopolist. That asymmetry deserves a real, if small, position — with the capital preserved for a better price.

---

## 4. Portfolio Fit Analysis

| Dimension | Finding | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| **Sector / correlation block** | **EFX–TRU 0.856**; EFX–SPGI 0.544, MCO 0.554, VRSK 0.493. Quant's 0.859 is confirmed independently | **This is one trade, not five.** Cap the information-services / credit-data sleeve at **5% of portfolio** with **EFX+TRU combined ≤3%**. If TRU is already held, start EFX at 0.5%, not 1.0% |
| **Market correlation** | EFX–SPY only **0.178**; R² 0.031 | 97% idiosyncratic. EFX is **not** a beta-completion or hedging tool. It is a concentrated idiosyncratic bet on one policy outcome — govern it with a name-level loss budget, not a beta overlay |
| **Beta conflict** | 0.59 (1yr calc) vs 1.34 (2yr vendor). Use **1.2–1.3** for downside planning | Do not let a low measured beta justify a larger weight |
| **Factor tilts added** | **Value (+), Quality (+), Momentum (−), High Vol (−)** | Deliberate anti-momentum position. Acceptable if intentional; if the book is momentum- or vol-targeted, this must be explicitly flagged as a factor bet |
| **Rate / duration** | Long-duration, mortgage-linked; 60–100bp revenue drag from a stronger USD | **Adds** correlated risk if the book already holds banks, homebuilders, mortgage insurers, or consumer lenders. **Partially hedges** a bond-proxy/defensive sleeve if the 10Y falls |
| **Classification trap** | FMP tags EFX "Industrials / Consulting Services" | **Exclude EFX from any Industrials sleeve count.** Booking it as industrial exposure would double-count a rate-sensitive data utility |
| **Liquidity** | 1.0–4.0M shares/day, $20.7B cap | Non-issue. Can build 2.5% over 2–3 sessions |

---

## 5. Entry Strategy — **SCALE IN, do not chase**

The single most important tactical fact: EFX closed at $137.01 intraday on 30-Sep and at **$176.54 on 20-Oct — +28.6% in 14 sessions, including an +11.3% single-day gap on 4.0M shares (2.5x normal).** That gap has not been tested. Consensus PT (~$174–175) sits *below* spot. Value's base IV ($170) sits *below* spot. **You are being asked to pay full price two weeks into a violent reversal.**

| Tranche | Size | Trigger | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| **T1 — Now** | 0.5% | Market, or limit **≤$168** | Establishes the position and the monitoring discipline. A limit at $168 captures the 19-Oct close ($158.57) to 20-Oct open ($166.11) gap-fill zone |
| **T2** | +0.75% | **≤$155** | Broken Jan-26 support; midpoint of the Sept collapse range; ~9% below base IV |
| **T3** | +0.75% | **≤$140** — *or* FY27 guide ≥8% revenue growth with margin expansion at the 3-Feb-27 print | Value's aggressive-buy level; also the 2-Oct close. Catalyst-triggered alternative lets you pay up only if the thesis is confirmed |

**Rules:** (a) **Do not exceed 1.0% before the 3-Feb-2027 Q4/FY27-guide print** — recent earnings-day gaps of 8–12% make this the year's largest single gap-risk event. (b) The FHFA NPRM is unscheduled and can move the stock 15–25% in a day (as on 29-Sep). Keep dry powder for that headline; do not pre-position for it. (c) Use limit orders throughout — bid/ask and gap behaviour in this name are wide.

---

## 6. Risk Management Rules

**Price stop: $131 close-basis (−26% from entry).**
Honest caveat: for a 44%-vol stock, a 26% stop is only ~0.6 standard deviations — it is a **discipline device, not a protection device**. The real protection is the 1.0% starting weight, which caps a full stop-out at ~0.26% of portfolio. Do not tighten the stop toward $155–160; at this volatility that is pure noise-harvesting.

**Thesis invalidation — exit on any of these, regardless of price:**
1. **FHFA finalizes a bi-merge / two-bureau rule** — a structural cut to revenue-per-origination across USIS *and* Mortgage Solutions. Cut to ≤0.5% or zero and reassess from scratch.
2. **USIS mortgage revenue turns negative YoY while the mortgage market is not shrinking** — this is share *loss*, and it destroys the thesis's single strongest pillar (Q3 mortgage +15% into a −20% market).
3. **Workforce Solutions organic growth <5% for two consecutive quarters**, or an adverse CFPB/FTC action against The Work Number. This segment is the entire operating income.
4. **FY27 revenue growth guided below 7%** at the 3-Feb-27 print — breaks the 8–12% long-term framework and the 20.8x forward multiple.
5. **Gross margin below 55% for two quarters** — score-price commoditization (VantageScore at $1 through 2028, TRU at 99¢) running ahead of unit-volume offset.
6. **Net debt/EBITDA >3.0x while buybacks continue** — the capital-allocation policy has already run at 128% of FCF; that converting into leverage is the balance-sheet failure mode.
7. **Goodwill impairment in Workforce Solutions** — confirms acquisition capital earned sub-par returns on 68% of assets.

**Trim triggers:**
- **$205–210 (~1.2x base IV, ~21x FY27 EPS $9.84):** trim one-third. At this level you are being paid full value for a narrow-moat asset.
- **$225–230 or ≥24x forward EPS:** trim to a ≤0.75% core, or exit. The 24-multiple historically required wide-moat characteristics EFX no longer has.
- **Re-rating without fundamental confirmation** (multiple >22x with no FY28 framework upgrade): trim mechanically.

**Review cadence:** 3-Feb-27 (Q4 + FY27 guide), Q1-27 print, Dec-26/Jan-27 FCRA settlement final approvals, Q4-26 close of Círculo de Crédito ($750M EV — watch goodwill, already +$1.18B in Q3), and any FHFA NPRM.

---

## 7. Final Portfolio Action: **INITIATE (starter 1.0%, pre-authorized ladder to 2.5%)**

**The one-line thesis:** *A narrow-moat data oligopolist with a genuinely irreplaceable asset (The Work Number) trading at ~12.8x EBITDA and ~20.8x forward EPS after a 41% drawdown — where the discount is roughly correctly priced by a live federal rulemaking that can re-cut the core mortgage product's economics.*

**Why Initiate and not Pass:** Zero agents allege fraud, the balance sheet is investment grade with the 2026/27 refinancing cliff neutralized, FCF is $1.1B and durable, and the sector cycle (US mortgage originations) is in late-trough. The bear case is bounded at −22% to a tested $137; the bull case is +25% to $220 on a mere 100bp retrace in the 10Y.

**Why not Add in size:** Price sits **above** Value's base IV, **at** consensus PT, and 28.6% above the 30-Sep low. There is no margin of safety at $176.54, and the market has already begun buying the disinflation scenario — meaning the "surprise" Macro identifies is partly in the tape.

**What would move me to Add aggressively:** price ≤$155, or an FY27 guide ≥8% revenue growth with margin expansion, or a clean resolution of the FHFA bi-merge proceeding. Any two of the three justifies the full 2.5%.

**What would move me to Exit:** an FHFA bi-merge final rule. That is the one event where I would not wait for price confirmation — the structural change to revenue-per-unit is permanent, and no amount of mortgage-volume recovery offsets it.

**Data gaps carried into this recommendation:** price feed ends 20-Oct-26; beta conflict (0.59 vs 1.34) unresolved — I used 1.2–1.3; Moody's current rating unconfirmed (S&P 'BBB' confirmed); FHFA covenant thresholds assumed ~3.5x, not verified; the Q3-26 acquisition terms inferred from the goodwill step-up rather than confirmed.

## SECTOR BRIEF — EQUIFAX INC. (NYSE: EFX)

**Classification note:** FMP tags EFX as *Industrials / Consulting Services*. That is a data artifact. EFX is one of the three US consumer credit bureaus — a subscription-plus-transaction risk-data and analytics business. Benchmarking it against Caterpillar and Boeing would be meaningless, so I benchmark both ways: against the assigned Industrials aggregate (for compliance) and against the true risk-data comp set (Experian, TransUnion, Verisk, FICO, CoStar).

---

### 1. Sector Overview

The credit bureau / risk-data sector is a mature, high-barrier oligopoly now overlaying a structural growth layer (identity, fraud, employment/income verification, government eligibility). The US credit agency market is roughly **$19.9B in 2026, growing ~6% CAGR toward ~$26B**; the three bureaus — Experian (~$8.5B revenue), Equifax ($6.6B TTM) and TransUnion ($4.6B) — control the overwhelming majority of US consumer credit data, with a de facto HHI well above 2,500. Barriers are extreme: proprietary data contributory networks (lenders supply data only to bureaus), FCRA/regulatory licensing, and deep embedding in lenders' underwriting workflows and model validation. Revenue is annuity-like (subscription/contract) but has one highly cyclical appendage — US mortgage origination — which is currently the sector's swing factor.

Against the *assigned* Industrials aggregate (25 largest names, FY2025: $822.0B revenue, 30.6% gross margin, $79.5B net income = 9.7% net margin), EFX is a structurally superior business: **55.2% gross margin vs 30.6%**, **11.3% net margin vs 9.7%**. EFX's economics resemble a data monopolist, not an industrial.

---

### 2. Key Tailwinds

- **Mortgage recovery optionality is un-priced.** Originations sit near a multi-year trough (BofA models 2027 originations ~$1.72T with elevated rates, weak refis, subdued resale). EFX grew mortgage revenue **+15% in Q3'26 despite a weakening market** — i.e., share gain and pricing, not volume. Every incremental refi/purchase dollar drops through at very high incremental margin.
- **Government/verification is the new structural leg.** EFX booked **$550M of annual contract value in state-agency signings** — Medicaid/work-requirement income verification built on The Work Number. This is contracted, less cyclical, and largely a volume-of-eligibility story tied to policy, not credit.
- **Pricing power + cost inflection.** Three-player structure supports annual pricing. The EFX Cloud migration is reaching completion, so the cloud D&A burden ($196M/quarter = 11.6% of revenue) should stop growing faster than revenue, unlocking GAAP operating-margin recovery toward the 2021 peak of 23.1%. FHFA's approval of VantageScore 4.0 also injects score-provider competition — the bureaus co-own VantageScore, so bureau data volumes benefit even as FICO's score economics face pressure.

### 3. Key Headwinds

- **US mortgage is EFX's largest single cyclical exposure** and is deteriorating: Q3'26 revenue landed *below* the July guidance midpoint on a **$20M US mortgage impact**, forcing a 2026 outlook cut. EFX is more mortgage-levered than Verisk or FICO.
- **Regulatory and legal overhang.** FCRA litigation, CFPB scrutiny of data-broker pricing and dispute handling, and proliferating state privacy statutes that raise data-acquisition cost and complexity. Adverse credit-reporting rulemaking is the sector's tail risk.
- **Consumer credit normalization.** Mortgage delinquency reached **4.44% in Q1'26 (+18bps YoY)**; delinquencies are stabilizing at a higher level, which makes lenders cautious on new origination — the opposite of what bureau transaction revenue needs.
- **Margin structure lags peers.** GAAP operating margin of 18.8% versus a 34.6% peer median is partly accounting/mix, but it is also real: heavy SGA ($390M/qtr) and cloud amortization keep EFX's EBITDA margin (30.4%) below Verisk (48.3%) and FICO (47.8%), roughly matching TransUnion (31.8%).

---

### 4. Peer Comparison

| Company | Mkt Cap | Revenue | Rev growth | Gross mgn | Op mgn | Net mgn | P/E | EV/EBITDA |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Equifax (EFX)** | $20.7B | $6.59B TTM | **+11.4%** TTM / +6.9% FY25 | 55.2% | 18.8% | 11.3% | 28.5x | **~12.8x** |
| Experian (EXPGY) | $34.5B | $8.47B FY-Mar26 | +12.6% | 38.6% | 25.4% | 17.8% | 22.9x | ~12.7x |
| TransUnion (TRU) | $15.0B | $4.58B FY25 | +9.4% | 59.1% | 18.7% | 10.0% | 33.7x | ~13.8x |
| Verisk (VRSK) | $24.8B | $3.07B FY25 | +6.6% | 69.9% | 43.7% | 29.6% | 29.4x | ~18.7x |
| Fair Isaac (FICO) | $17.3B | $1.99B FY-Sep25 | +15.9% | 82.2% | 46.5% | 32.7% | 30.1x | ~20.5x |
| CoStar (CSGP) | $13.4B | $3.25B FY25 | +18.7% | 75.2% | -2.2% | neg. | n/m | n/m |
| **Peer median (ex-CSGP)** | — | — | **+11.4%** | **64.5%** | **34.6%** | **23.7%** | **29.8x** | **~16.3x** |

*EV/EBITDA uses net debt estimated from reported interest expense (~5% implied cost) — flagged as approximate. P/E on GAAP diluted EPS; EFX's adjusted EPS is materially higher ($2.26 adj. vs $1.80 GAAP in Q3'26), so on adjusted earnings EFX screens cheaper than 28.5x.*

**Read-through:** EFX is *at parity on growth* (+11.4% vs +11.4% median) and is visibly outgrowing its closest twin TransUnion (+9.4%) — a share-gain signal in the US. It is *below* the median on every margin line, and trades at a ~20% discount on EV/EBITDA (12.8x vs 16.3x median) — a discount that is essentially a margin-quality discount, not a growth discount.

---

### 5. Target Company's Competitive Position: **STRONG** (franchise) / **AVERAGE** (profitability)

**Rationale — why strong:** EFX holds an irreplaceable data asset inside a three-firm oligopoly, has re-accelerated TTM revenue growth to 11.4% (above TransUnion and above the 5-year 9.6% CAGR), and is winning share in mortgage despite a shrinking market. The $550M state-contract ACV win demonstrates genuine pricing/product optionality beyond credit data. Beta of 1.34 and ~15,000 employees understate the annuity quality of the revenue base.

**Rationale — where it lags:** Operating margin of 18.8% sits 16 points below the peer median and 4 points below its own 2021 level (23.1%); net margin of 11.3% is roughly half the peer median. The EFX Cloud program consumed years of margin and still carries $196M/quarter of D&A. Until that leverage shows up in GAAP operating margin, EFX deserves to trade at a discount to Verisk and FICO. Watch adjusted EBITDA margin (currently 30.4%) as the scorecard for whether the cloud spend was value-accretive.

**Net:** A top-tier competitive asset producing second-quartile financial returns — a margin-recovery story rather than a moat-deficit story.

## 1. ESG Materiality Map

For a credit bureau, the ESG value drivers are unusual: environmental factors are largely immaterial, while **social (data security, data accuracy) and governance (cyber oversight, regulatory conduct) factors are the business model itself.** A credit bureau's product *is* other people's personal data; misuse, inaccuracy or breach is simultaneously a social harm and a revenue/liability event.

| **Regulatory (FCRA / GDPR / EU AI Act)** | **Critical** | Licence to operate; data-scope rules change the addressable data set. |

## 2. Environmental Risk Assessment: **LOW**

- **Carbon intensity:** Low and structurally declining. The "Equifax Cloud" migration (largely complete) consolidated on-premise data centres onto hyperscaler infrastructure, which is the primary driver of both emissions and cost reduction — a rare case where the ESG lever and the margin lever are the same lever.
- **Targets:** Net-zero by 2040 with **SBTi-validated** interim targets (announced 2021); TCFD-aligned Climate Report published annually (2025 edition confirms a refreshed climate risk/opportunity register reviewed by the Board).
- **Weakness:** CDP climate **not disclosed** — the one environmental transparency gap versus European peers. Scope 3 (purchased cloud, capital goods) is the dominant category and is estimated rather than measured.
- **Physical climate risk:** Minimal. No manufacturing, no water-intensive process, no commodity input. The only physical vector is data-centre/utility reliability, which is a business-continuity issue more than a climate one.
- **Transition risk:** No carbon-tax or CBAM exposure of consequence; CBAM is irrelevant to a services exporter.
- **Controversies:** None material. No spills, fines or remediation liabilities identified.

**Verdict:** Environmental is ESG's least interesting dimension here — which is itself useful, because it means management attention is not diverted. Cheap to be good at.

## 3. Social Risk Assessment: **HIGH**

This is where Equifax carries a genuine, permanent risk premium.

**(a) Data security — the defining event.** The 2017 breach exposed personal data of ~147 million consumers (SSNs, birth dates, addresses, some driver's licence and credit-card data) after an unpatched Apache Struts vulnerability went un-remediated. The global settlement with the FTC, CFPB and all 50 states reached **up to $700M** ($425M consumer restitution fund, $175M to states, $100M CFPB civil penalty), with a **20-year consent order** mandating a comprehensive information-security programme and third-party assessments. Cumulative pre-tax breach costs exceeded **$1.2–1.4B** once legal, remediation, insurance and technology transformation are aggregated — against a market cap that was ~$17B at the time. This was a company-defining, not a peripheral, event, and it triggered the CEO transition (Mark Begor, April 2018) and the entire cloud re-platforming.

**(b) Product accuracy / FCRA — the chronic, under-priced risk.** Post-breach, the recurring social liability is *inaccuracy*, not hacking:
- A **2022 coding error** caused incorrect credit scores to be furnished to lenders for a period of months (~300,000 consumers affected per company disclosure; plaintiffs alleged millions of scores). Resulted in a **~$100M class settlement**.
- Continuous flow of individual and class FCRA actions alleging mixed/duplicate collection accounts, re-aged tradelines and failure to conduct reasonable reinvestigation. A recent plaintiff verdict found actual damages plus a punitive award on a **willfulness** finding — the dangerous outcome, because FCRA statutory damages of $100–$1,000 per consumer per violation aggregate to nine figures at bureau scale.
- Active 2026 litigation includes a Philadelphia class action over inaccurate reports and a federal action naming both Equifax and Experian (mid-2026).

**(c) Financial inclusion — the genuine positive.** Equifax is a commercial beneficiary of extending credit visibility to thin-file consumers, and state/agency verification contracts ($550M ACV) are sticky, mission-aligned revenue.

**(d) Workforce.** 15,000 employees; the 2024–26 "productivity initiatives" driving margin expansion imply headcount discipline and elevated restructuring/attrition. No significant union, safety or supply-chain labour exposure — Workforce Solutions' verification products consume employment data but do not depend on low-cost labour.

**Verdict:** High, and structurally so. This is not a company that can ever de-risk its social profile — only manage it. Note the asymmetry: the 2017 breach is now a *known* cost that management has spent nine years and >$1.5B addressing; the FCRA accuracy tail is *unknown* and recurring.

EFX has round-tripped from a May-2025 high of ~$276 to a **30 September 2026 trough of $137 (−50%)**, before rebounding **+11% to $176.54** on a Q3'26 beat (revenue $1.693B, +10%; adj. No new ESG shock occurred in 2026.

**Therefore the correct weight on ESG in the thesis is as a persistent discount-rate and tail-risk input, not a catalyst:**

- **Positive:** Deregulatory CFPB posture (data-broker rule withdrawn, medical-debt rule vacated, FCRA preemption reaffirmed) removes near-term data-scope risk. SBTi-validated net-zero and independent chair make EFX investable for most ESG-screened mandates. Financial-inclusion revenue is real and growing.
- **Negative:** The FCRA accuracy tail is unquantified and recurring; the EU AI Act imposes new high-risk-AI compliance cost on EU operations from 2026; state privacy fragmentation is the rising risk that federal preemption may not hold; and compensation still lacks a cyber/accuracy modifier.
- **Valuation read-through:** Assign a modest ESG/governance discount to the multiple — roughly 0.5–1.0x EBITDA — reflecting the un-insurable nature of the data-integrity tail rather than any environmental exposure. At $176.54 the market is not pricing an ESG premium *or* an ESG penalty; the de-rating is cyclical.

**Bottom line: ESG is not a reason to own or avoid EFX. It is a reason to size the position for a low-probability, high-severity operational event, and to press management on adding a data-accuracy/cyber metric to the incentive plan — the cheapest available reduction in tail risk.**
